limitations: Predictions describe an average pilot with the sleep and duty times entered; individuals differ (90th-percentile values are shown for reference). The published reference model has residual error of about 1.42 KSS units; AeroWake has not been independently validated.
The model does not account for sleep disorders, illness, medication, caffeine, workload, stress or commuting beyond what is entered as sleep and duty times.
This report supports, and does not replace, the pilot’s own judgement of fitness for duty. It is not a medical assessment.
Regulatory references are to Regulation (EU) 965/2012 (EASA ORO.FTL); operator schemes may differ.

narrative.title: Event
narrative.text: The pilot reported being unfit for duty due to fatigue before the duty Tue 08 Sep 05:30 EZY801/802/803 LGW → EDI → LGW → EDI (home-base time, Europe/London). The recorded event or concern time is Tue 08 Sep 04:30 (08 Sep 03:30Z).

narrative.title: Sleep
narrative.text: 3 sleep period(s) totalling 16h45 were provided, including sleep before the reporting period (3 reported by the pilot, 0 estimated from the roster). Before the event there were 5h00 of sleep in 24 h, 11h15 in 48 h and 16h45 in 72 h; last wake Tue 08 Sep 04:15, about 0h15 awake at the event. The supplied pattern contains 4h00 of sleep in the 24 h before duty report at Tue 08 Sep 05:30, and 11h00 in the 48 h before; estimated time awake at that point is 1h15.

narrative.title: Duties
narrative.text: 3 duty period(s) in the selected period, 2 operated. Shortest rest between duties: 4h45. Disruptive elements: Mon 07 Sep 14:00 EZY1 LGW → FCO → LGW (late finish); Tue 08 Sep 05:30 EZY801/802/803 LGW → EDI → LGW → EDI (early start).

narrative.title: Predicted alertness
narrative.text: Had the duty been operated, predicted sleepiness is KSS 6.4 at the start and peaks at KSS 6.4 (“Some signs of sleepiness”) at Tue 08 Sep 05:30; KSS 5.8 at the final landing. For a more fatigue-susceptible pilot (90th percentile) the peak would be about KSS 7.5. The pilot would have been awake about 9h45 by the end.

narrative.title: Pilot assessment
narrative.text: At Tue 08 Sep 04:30 the pilot rated themselves KSS 8 (“Sleepy, some effort to keep awake”) and Samn-Perelli 6 (“Extremely tired, very difficult to concentrate”). The model predicted KSS 6.4 at that time.

narrative.text: Crew position: First officer. Mitigations taken: Caffeine, Informed crew control / duty manager. Effect on the operation: Duty not operated. Suggested action: Review late-to-early transitions on this pairing.

narrative.title: Conclusion
narrative.text: Main issues identified: pilot reports significant fatigue; prior sleep/wake check failed on multiple criteria; less than 5 h sleep in the 24 h before the duty; less than 12 h sleep in the 48 h before the duty; rest shorter than the regulatory minimum; late finish followed by early start.
